headline: MIT mathematics students say OpenAI's published proofs, including a claimed solution to a famous Millennium Prize Problem, have left them fearing for their careers.
score_reason: Pool score kept: strong first-hand reporting, but a small survey and OpenAI's proofs are not yet checked.
importance_line: Early-career mathematicians fear fewer academic jobs, but the survey is small (45 of 120 responded) and the accuracy of OpenAI’s proofs is still being sorted out.
summary: The Boston Globe reports that after OpenAI said on 8 Sep 2026 that its AI agents solved a Millennium Prize Problem (one of the famous maths puzzles that each carry a $1 million prize) and later published proofs for nearly 400 more, MIT’s maths department held a meeting to discuss AI. In a department survey (45 of 120 students responded), three in four feared AI would make a tenure-track job harder to get and 71 percent were looking to pivot away from academic maths, while the Globe notes the accuracy of the proofs is still to be sorted out.
notes: Dates in the Globe article are internally unclear (meeting “two days” after 8 Sep, proofs “last week”); the entry uses only OpenAI’s 8 Sep announcement date as the Globe gives it.
